beats.intro: An equation like y equals x plus three is a line. [[q]]An inequality like y is less than x plus three is a whole region of the plane.
beats.boundary: To graph y is less than x plus three, [[eq]]first pretend it's an equation: y equals x plus three. [[line]]Graph that line. It's the boundary of the region. [[ask]]Next, decide: solid or dashed? [[lt]]With less than or greater than, points on the line are not included, so the line is dashed, just like an open circle on a number line. [[le]]With less than or equal to, or greater than or equal to, points on the line are included, so the line is solid, like a closed circle.
beats.test: The line splits the plane into two sides. All the solutions are on one side. [[pt]]To find out which, test a point. Zero, zero is the easiest. [[chk]]Is zero less than zero plus three? Yes, zero is less than three. [[shade]]So shade the side that contains zero, zero. [[more]]Any point in the shaded region works. Try two, one: one is less than five. [[bad]]A point on the other side, like negative four, three, fails: three is not less than negative one.
beats.q1: Quick check. Graph y is greater than or equal to negative two x plus one.
beats.ex2: Here's another: six x minus two y is greater than or equal to five. [[solve]]Solve for y. Subtract six x: negative two y is greater than or equal to negative six x plus five. [[flip]]Divide by negative two, and remember to flip the sign: y is less than or equal to three x minus five halves. [[line]]The sign includes equal, so the boundary is solid. [[test]]Test zero, zero in the original: six times zero minus two times zero is zero, and zero is not greater than or equal to five. [[shade]]Zero, zero is not a solution, so shade the other side. [[below]]That's the region below the line, which matches y is less than or equal to.
beats.q2: Quick check. Pick any point that is a solution.
beats.special: Some boundaries are horizontal or vertical. [[h]]For y is greater than negative five, draw a dashed horizontal line at negative five, [[hs]]and shade above it: every point with a y value greater than negative five. [[v]]For x is less than or equal to two, draw a solid vertical line at two, [[vs]]and shade to the left.
beats.wrap: To graph a linear inequality, [[w1]]graph the boundary line: dashed for less than or greater than, solid when equal is included. [[w2]]Test a point that's not on the line, often zero, zero. [[w3]]If it works, shade its side. If not, shade the other side. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final2: Next, decide whether each point is a solution.
beats.final3: Last one. Solve each inequality for y.
beats.finish: Well done. That's the end of chapter thirty-seven, graphing linear inequalities.
